en: One night, a lake killed more than 1,700 people,
and almost none of them were even in the water.
August 21st, 1986,
Cameroon.
Families were living peacefully
near a beautiful lake called Lake Nyos.
But that night, something terrifying happened.
An enormous invisible cloud began spreading from the lake,
flowing down into nearby villages.
People suddenly collapsed.
Animals dropped to the ground, and by morning,
entire communities had been devastated.
But here's the strange part.
There was no fire, no lava, and no visible sign
of what had killed them.
So what actually happened?
Scientists eventually discovered something extraordinary.
Deep beneath the lake, enormous amounts
of carbon dioxide had been building up for years.
And on that night, the trapped gas suddenly escaped.
A deadly cloud swept into the valleys,
filling the air with dangerous concentrations of carbon dioxide.
More than 1,700 people lost their lives.
But here's what makes this story even more disturbing.
Just two years earlier, another lake
in Cameroon had released deadly gas.
37 people died, and almost nobody imagined that something
far worse was coming.
After the disaster, engineers installed special pipes
to release the trapped gas more safely.
Today, Lake Nyos still exists.
Its waters look peaceful.
Its surroundings are beautiful.
But underneath that calm surface once hid one
of the deadliest natural surprises in modern history.
File One, The Unknown File.
